title: Vasubandhu's Treasury of Abhidharma — the Sanskrit text
textType: Verses with an auto-commentary in prose
author: vasubandhu
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vasubandhu, the great abhidharma master who turned afterwards to the Yogācāra; the root verses are his own and the prose that follows them is his commentary on them, in which he reports the views of the Vaibhāṣika school and answers them from the Sautrāntika position. The e-text follows the edition of P. Pradhan (Patna 1975, Tibetan Sanskrit Works Series 8) and its source is recorded by GRETIL as unknown; it was input by the Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon Input Project.
description: The Abhidharmakośa is the great summa of Buddhist scholasticism: its eight kośas treat the elements of experience and the faculties, the functioning of the mind and the mental states, the structure of the world and its beings, the karma that produces the world, the latencies that bind beings to it, the paths and the persons who walk them, the knowledges won on the way, and the meditative attainments that end in the destruction of the defilements. Each verse is followed by the prose of the author, so the reader has both the mnemonic and the argument on one page.
historicalContext: Vasubandhu's Treasury reorganised the Sarvāstivāda teaching and became the standard abhidharma of the Sanskrit, Chinese and Tibetan schools; its Chinese translation by Xuanzang and its Tibetan translation made it the foundation of the monastic curriculum, and it remains the clearest account of what Buddhist scholasticism held the world to be.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: all eight kośasthānas with Vasubandhu's own commentary on each verse, 598 passages, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one kośasthāna at a time. The file prints the work's title, the name of the first kośasthāna and its homage above the opening verses, and the reader drops them. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
